issues_resolved: Initial recovery interpreter filter still treated arbitrary Python/R input arguments as executing scripts; author replaced it with actual script-operand recognition.
Final review identified Python stdin and R -e/--args edge cases; these are now recognized as non-file invocations and regression-tested.

runtime_scope.inspection: Pinned Rscript wrapper uses exec to replace itself with the R executable, preserving the active subprocess PID. Exclusion of that owned PID therefore covers actual launched study chains; no assumption of automatic arbitrary descendant exclusion is made.
runtime_scope.limitations: The process guard recognizes the file-based interpreter invocations used by this study, not arbitrary scripts dynamically sourced through -c/-e/-m or unrelated compute. Root must separately avoid concurrent unrelated CPU-intensive workloads.
runtime_scope.preserved: Scientific chain and diagnostic wrappers, fixed model/data identity, runtime pin set, outcome denominators, cgroup ancestor constraints, pilot RSS policy, timeout handling and cleanup mechanics unchanged. m.validate() passed without invoking R.

budget.basis: Four2320-second chain caps, plus five-second cleanup allowance per chain, plus all previous cancelled-chain elapsed times. Prior record agrees with original ledger.
budget.limitations: This is nominal chain-process accounting, not an absolute all-phase wall bound: dispatcher polling/guard/scheduling overhead may add elapsed time, and preparation120s plus diagnostics300s are separate allocations. The ~8.47-second margin is small. Preserve and report actual elapsed times; no automatic extra allocation if the cap or convergence gate fails.
budget.completion: 2320 seconds per chain is near the prior runtime projection, so fixed48000 retention may not complete. Timeout/cancelled/not_launched outcomes remain scientifically unresolved, not successes.
